boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission outdoor and public-library activities for a Louisville day with friends.

cards.title: Walk Central Park’s paths
cards.subtitle: Old Louisville · 1340 S. 4th St.
cards.notes: Meet at the Fourth Street entrance, take a lap on the walking paths, then use the benches and lawns for a low-key catch-up.
cards.short_summary: An Olmsted park with paths, lawns, seating, and public amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Olmsted Parks lists Central Park’s walking paths, playgrounds, stages, tennis courts, restrooms, and 6 a.m.–11 p.m. hours; its master-plan material describes Olmsted Parks as providing free recreation opportunities.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for a park walk; observe posted park rules and hours.

cards.title: Walk, run, or bike Car-Free Cherokee
cards.subtitle: Cherokee Park · monthly Sunday closure
cards.notes: Pick a designated Car-Free Cherokee Sunday and make the Scenic Loop your route; bring water and share the path with other users.
cards.short_summary: A recurring vehicle-free morning for walking, running, and biking.
cards.evidence_claim: Olmsted Parks Conservancy and Louisville Parks and Recreation close Cherokee Park’s Scenic Loop to vehicle traffic one Sunday each month, 8 a.m.–2 p.m., for walking, running, and biking; Olmsted Parks provide free recreation opportunities.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required; check the current monthly date before traveling.

cards.title: Take the North Overlook route
cards.subtitle: Iroquois Park · 2120 Rundill Rd.
cards.notes: Use the marked park roads and trails to reach the North Overlook, pause for the view, and head back before dusk with your group.
cards.short_summary: A named overlook in Louisville’s historic Iroquois Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisville Metro Parks identifies the North Overlook as an Iroquois Park feature; Olmsted Parks’ materials describe its parks as providing free recreation opportunities.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for the outdoor park visit; use established routes and posted rules.

cards.title: Set up a park meet-up at Shawnee
cards.subtitle: West Louisville · 4501 W. Broadway
cards.notes: Choose a visible open area, bring a ball or a book you already own, and use the park as a free place to spend time together.
cards.short_summary: A named Olmsted park with public outdoor space.
cards.evidence_claim: Olmsted Parks Conservancy lists Shawnee Park at 4501 W. Broadway and describes the Olmsted Parks as providing free recreation and community-gathering opportunities.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for ordinary park use; follow posted rules.

cards.title: Hit on free clay courts
cards.subtitle: Chickasaw Park · 1200 Southwestern Pkwy.
cards.notes: Bring rackets and balls you already have, check the courts on arrival, and rotate courteously if others are waiting to play.
cards.short_summary: Louisville Metro identifies these as the region’s only free clay tennis courts.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisville Metro Parks states that Chickasaw Park, on Southwestern Parkway, features the region’s only free clay tennis courts.
cards.source_title: Park Improvement Projects and Master Plans — Louisville Metro Parks
cards.access_notes: Court use is identified by Louisville Metro as free; bring your own equipment and follow posted court guidance.

cards.title: Make a simple Stansbury Park stop
cards.subtitle: Old Louisville · 2302 S. 3rd St.
cards.notes: Use this smaller named park as a daylight conversation stop, then continue on foot toward nearby campus or Old Louisville destinations.
cards.short_summary: A named Olmsted park on South Third Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Olmsted Parks Conservancy lists Stansbury Park at 2302 S. 3rd St. and describes the Olmsted Parks as providing free recreation and community-gathering opportunities.
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for ordinary park use; visit during daylight and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Catch Waterfront Wednesday on the lawn
cards.subtitle: Big Four Lawn · Waterfront Park
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or use the lawn space for the concert; food vendors are optional, so the live music itself does not require a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free concert series staged on Waterfront Park’s Big Four Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisville Public Media states that Waterfront Wednesday shows on the Big Four Lawn in Waterfront Park are free.
cards.access_notes: Concert admission is free; optional food, vendor purchases, transportation, and parking are separate.

cards.title: Walk the Beckley Creek trails
cards.subtitle: The Parklands of Floyds Fork
cards.notes: Choose a trail length that fits your group, use the Parklands maps before leaving, and stay on marked routes for an easy outdoor hang.
cards.short_summary: A named Parklands destination with access to the Floyds Fork trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: The Parklands says its more than 4,000 acres and trails are free and open to all 365 days a year.
cards.source_title: Adventure, Discovery, and Relaxation Await This Summer at The Parklands
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for park access; use current trail information and posted safety guidance.

cards.title: Explore Pope Lick Park’s trails
cards.subtitle: The Parklands of Floyds Fork
cards.notes: Plan a daytime trail walk with friends, use a map to select a route, and avoid leaving marked paths or entering restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: A named Parklands destination for a map-guided outdoor walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Parklands says its more than 4,000 acres and trails are free and open to all 365 days a year.
cards.source_title: Adventure, Discovery, and Relaxation Await This Summer at The Parklands
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required for park access; stick to official trails and observe closures.

cards.title: Make something at an LFPL makerspace
cards.subtitle: Participating Louisville Free Public Library locations
cards.notes: Complete the required orientation, reserve time where needed, and work on a small project using the library’s shared tools and equipment.
cards.short_summary: Library maker spaces provide tools for collaborative making and learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisville Free Public Library says its makerspaces are free and open to active LFPL cardholders; adults and teens 13+ must complete Maker 101 orientation before using equipment.
cards.access_notes: Free for active LFPL cardholders; Maker 101 orientation and any location-specific reservation requirements apply.
